column1: # models.catalog.tsv - the model families and variants the chooser offers, best -> smallest
# WITHIN each family (this order is the quality ranking curation relies on). Columns:
# The two optional trailing columns declare a llama.cpp-served model: engine "gguf" plus the
# one quant file to download from the repo (a GGUF repo holds many quants; the row prices and
# fetches ONLY that file). Omitted = engine mlx, whole-repo download. Because one GGUF repo
# holds every quant, a gguf row's repo_name column is the UNIQUE INSTALL NAME (the Models/
# directory the file lands in, also what the display label is parsed from), and the gguf_file
# column carries "actual_repo/file.gguf" - the real Hugging Face repo joined to the quant file
# (which must sit at the repo root). A gguf_file without a "/" means repo_name IS the repo.
# Lines starting with # are ignored. A repo that does not exist (yet) on Hugging Face is
# skipped silently by the catalog fetch, so planned-but-unpublished conversions can stay
# listed here and light up the moment they are uploaded. When publishing MiLMMT conversions
# under a different account, change the hf_author column here - nothing else references it.
